title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر لجمعية المرأة عن نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures for the Women's Association on Coming to the Aid of the Prophet, God Bless Him and Grant Him Peace
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مساء أمس الأربعاء فاتح محرم 1445هـ الموافق 19 يوليو 2023م محاضرة بعنوان" إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله " بدعوة وتنظيم من جمعية المرأة للتربية والثقافة.
وقد تحدث فضيلة الشيخ في محاضرته عن واجب النصرة ومسؤولية المسلمين تجاه نبيهم صلى الله عليه وسلم؛
مبينا أن الله تعالى نصر نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من قبل، وكفاه المستهزئين فقد كفاه شر كفار قريش، وحفظه في الغار كما حفظه في المواقف كلها، وقد توفى الله نبيه، وجعل أمانة نصرته في أعناق أمته إلى يوم القيامة، فمن نصره فله الأجر، ومن تولى فقد خذله الله.
وأشار الشيخ إلى أن نصرة النبي تتطلب أن يكون حاضرا في ذهن كل مسلم ولا يتأتى ذلك إلا بمعرفته صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يمكن معرفته إلا بتعلم سيرته والاقتداء بسنته واقتفاء أثره وسبيل ذلك استحضار نعمة الله سبحانه وتعالى ومنته على عباده المؤمنين.. مستعرضا نماذج من نصرة الصحابة والتابعين له عليه الصلاة والسلام.
مبينا الحكم الشرعي لساب النبي، وما يجب على حكام المسلمين فعله فيه نصرة للرسول الكريم صلى الله عليه وسلم، فالنصرة دليل محبة والمحبة دليل طاعة وكل محبوب مطاع.
body_en:
On the evening of yesterday, Wednesday the first of Muharram 1445 AH, corresponding to 19 July 2023, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a lecture entitled "If you do not aid him, then God has already aided him", at the invitation of and organised by the Women's Association for Upbringing and Culture.
In his lecture His Eminence the Sheikh spoke about the duty of coming to the Prophet's aid and the responsibility of the Muslims towards their Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace;
explaining that God Almighty aided His Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, in times past, and sufficed him against those who mocked him — for He sufficed him against the evil of the disbelievers of Quraysh — and protected him in the cave as He protected him in every situation; and that God then took His Prophet and placed the trust of coming to his aid upon the necks of his community until the Day of Resurrection: whoever comes to his aid has the reward, and whoever turns away, God has forsaken him.
The Sheikh indicated that coming to the Prophet's aid requires that he be present in the mind of every Muslim, and that this comes about only through knowing him, God bless him and grant him peace; and that he cannot be known except by learning his biography (sīrah), taking his sunnah as a model and following in his tracks — the way to which is to call to mind God's favour, glorified and exalted, and His kindness to His believing servants. He went over examples of how the Companions and the Successors came to his aid, upon him be blessings and peace.
He explained the Sharia ruling on one who reviles the Prophet, and what the rulers of the Muslims are obliged to do about him in coming to the aid of the noble Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace — for coming to his aid is evidence of love, and love is evidence of obedience, and everyone who is loved is obeyed.

flags.arabic: مبينا الحكم الشرعي لساب النبي، وما يجب على حكام المسلمين فعله فيه
flags.context: the report's closing sentence, summarising what the Sheikh said about one who reviles the Prophet
options: He explained the Sharia ruling on one who reviles the Prophet, and what the rulers of the Muslims are obliged to do about him
He set out the legal ruling concerning a person who insults the Prophet, and the duty of Muslim rulers regarding him
He clarified the ruling on blasphemy against the Prophet, and what Muslim heads of state must do about it
flags.note: Editorially the most sensitive sentence in the record. The report says only that the Sheikh explained a ruling and what rulers must do; it does not state what the ruling is. The English must not fill that in, and it does not. Option 2 is rejected: 'blasphemy' imports a Christian-law category the Arabic does not use, and 'heads of state' narrows ḥukkām. The pronoun فيه refers to the reviler, not to the act, and 'about him' keeps that.

translator_notes: A news report by the site's news desk summarising a lecture. Every point is the desk's summary of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and the site should present it as such.

The lecture title "إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله" is a fragment of Qur'an 9:40. Style guide section 4 asks for Qur'anic quotation in curly quotation marks with a reference, but here the phrase is functioning as the announced title of a lecture rather than as a quotation in running text, so it is rendered as a title. The site may prefer to mark it as scriptural. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and not a substitute for the Arabic.
نصرة is rendered 'coming to the aid of' throughout rather than 'victory' or 'support', so that the single Arabic word stays visible as one idea across the record.
The record attributes to the Sheikh a statement that rulers are obliged (yajib) to act; the obligation is reported, not issued here, and the attribution has been kept explicit.
editorial_review_reasons: The record reports that the Sheikh set out the Sharia ruling on one who reviles the Prophet and what Muslim rulers are obliged to do about him, without stating the ruling. Published in English under the Sheikh's name and without the lecture itself, a reader may supply the severest ruling in the tradition. In several Western jurisdictions that inference, presented as his position, carries reputational and potentially legal exposure for the publisher. The text has been translated faithfully and neither softened nor strengthened; whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.
